subject: general
question:
Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.

The burglar destroyed several items in the room. Even the carpet has been torn.

options.text: The burglar, being destroyed several items in the room, also carpet has torn.
Several items destroyed in the room by the burglar. Even the carpet he has torn.
Including the carpet, several items in the room have been torn by the burglar.
Several items in the room were destroyed by the burglar. Even the carpet has been torn.

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Passive voice structure: The object of the active voice sentence becomes the subject of the passive voice sentence.
 
• The first part of the active sentence is: "The burglar destroyed several items in the room." (Simple Past tense).
 
• To convert to passive voice: Move the object "several items in the room" to the subject position.
 
• Change the active verb "destroyed" to "were destroyed" (past simple passive for plural subjects).
 
• The second sentence "Even the carpet has been torn" is already in the passive voice (Present Perfect passive) and should remain unchanged.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Several items in the room were destroyed by the burglar. Even the carpet has been torn."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: **"The burglar, being destroyed..." – Uses an incorrect participial construction and the wrong tense.
 
• **Option 2: **"Several items destroyed..." – Missing the auxiliary verb "were," making the sentence grammatically incomplete.
 
• **Option 3: **"Including the carpet, several items... have been torn" – Changes the meaning by applying "torn" to all items, whereas the original used "destroyed."
